messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis? Usually, the standard error of the sample mean is s / sqrt(n). But they mention "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard error of the sampling distribution of the mean under null: sigma / sqrt(n). But we only have sample standard deviation, not population sigma. For t-test, we use sample standard deviation. So standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. So 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So standard deviation of the null hypothesis test (i.e., standard error) is about 0.2213.

But maybe they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? For t-test, the test statistic t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(n)). The denominator is the standard error. So the standard deviation of the null distribution of t is 1 (for t distribution with df=39). But they might want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean under null: that's the standard error. So answer: ~0.221.

Thus respond with calculation.
